papers.title: GenCAMO: Scene-Graph Contextual Decoupling for Environment-Aware and Mask-Free Camouflage Image–Dense Annotation Generation
papers.summary: Concealed dense prediction (CDP), including camouflaged object detection, RGB-D camouflaged object detection, and open-vocabulary camouflaged object segmentation, requires reasoning about objects whose appearance closely resembles their surroundings. Progress is constrained by the scarcity of diverse camouflage images with consistent pixel-level and multimodal annotations. Although generative models offer a promising source of training data, synthesizing useful camouflage supervision requires preserving object identity and scene geometry while adapting foreground appearance to the environment.

papers.title: 鸽子外纹体中颜色选择性神经元群体的神经表征
papers.summary: Understanding how birds encode object color is fundamental to elucidating the neural mechanisms of color vision. Although behavioral studies have shown high color-discrimination accuracy in birds, it remains unclear whether higher-order visual areas organize color information in a structured manner. Here, we performed multi-site multi-unit activity recordings from the pigeon entopallium while presenting multi-category images that systematically varied in hue, luminance, and saturation. Many entopallium sites exhibited robust hue selectivity that remained stable across luminance and saturation

papers.summary: Banana diseases cause significant crop losses worldwide and threaten food security in many tropical and subtropical regions. Accurate disease diagnosis remains challenging under real-world field conditions characterized by cluttered backgrounds, conditions far removed from laboratory-controlled environments. This paper presents Social-AgriNet, an explainable multimodal deep learning framework for robust banana disease detection from field-acquired imagery. Subpixel Camera-Based Structural Damage Identification with Physics-Guided Deep Learning
papers.summary: This independent technical research report presents a simulation-based framework for structural damage detection and localization using computer vision, finite element modeling, vibration analysis, and deep learning. The study integrates Euler–Bernoulli beam modeling, synthetic camera recordings, subpixel displacement tracking, natural-frequency and mode-shape estimation, and TensorFlow neural networks. The research comprises 35 computational experiments investigating hidden stiffness damage, camera measurement noise, motion magnification, environmental uncertainty, and damage identification.

papers.summary: Abstract Registration of longitudinal brain MRI scans containing pathologies remains a challenging problem, due to substantial changes in tissue appearance. To address this gap, we introduced the brain tumor sequence registration (BraTS-Reg) challenge, the first public benchmark specifically designed for deformable registration between pre-operative and follow-up scans of patients with adult-type diffuse gliomas.
